cashflowPrinciples.rule1: Cash is king — a profitable business can still fail if it runs out of cash. Revenue on a P&L is not cash in the bank.
cashflowPrinciples.rule2: Furniture businesses are cash-intensive: you pay suppliers before clients pay you. This gap must be managed actively.
cashflowPrinciples.rule3: Always maintain a minimum 8-week operating expense reserve in liquid accounts.
cashflowPrinciples.rule4: Never commit to a supplier order without a signed client deposit in hand — deposit funds the manufacturing commitment.

cashflowTimeline.dayZero: Client deposit received (30% of project value)
cashflowTimeline.day1to5: Supplier deposit paid (30% of supplier cost) — gap: TCD covers the difference between supplier cost and client deposit
cashflowTimeline.week6to8: Goods arrive in Australian warehouse — balance invoice raised to client
cashflowTimeline.week7to9: Client balance received (70% of project value) — project cash positive at this point
cashflowTimeline.week8to10: Supplier balance and freight invoice settled
cashflowTimeline.netCashPosition: TCD typically cash-neutral or cash-positive by 10 weeks from order — positive position accelerates with shorter lead times

cashflowRisks.multipleProjectsConcurrent: 3+ concurrent large projects can create cash strain — deposits out before balances in. Monitor weekly.
cashflowRisks.slowPayingClients: Late balance payment squeezes supplier payment window. Include 14-day payment terms on all balance invoices. Add 1.5%/month late payment clause.
cashflowRisks.supplierAdvancePayment: Some suppliers require higher deposits (50%+) — negotiate to standard 30/70 wherever possible
cashflowRisks.unforeseenCosts: Customs delays, damaged goods, re-delivery — always hold a 5% project contingency reserve in cash

accelerateDebtors: Invoice immediately on delivery completion — not end of month
Send reminder 3 days before due date (not on due date)
Offer 1% early payment discount for payment within 7 days on large invoices
Enable EFT, credit card (via Stripe), and BPAY payment methods — reduce friction
manageCreditorsStrategically: Pay suppliers on the last day of their agreed terms — not before
Negotiate 60-day terms with key suppliers as volume grows
Use supplier credit facilities where available to extend payment window
cashflowImprovement.forecastWeekly: Maintain a 13-week rolling cashflow forecast — update every Monday. Identify cash shortfalls 6–8 weeks before they occur.

weeklyKPIs.cashOnHand: Bank balance at close of business Friday
weeklyKPIs.debtorsOutstanding: Total receivables by age bucket (current / 30 / 60 / 90+ days)
weeklyKPIs.netCashPosition: Cash on hand + receivables due <30 days - payables due <14 days
weeklyKPIs.projectsOpenDeposit: Projects with deposit received but balance not yet invoiced — indicates upcoming inflow
